title: Any tips for cleaning up AI-generated assets?
author: RungerdH
selftext:
Hi!

I've run into a problem where more than half of my time working with assets is spent cleaning up color noise in generated images.  
At this point, it's sometimes faster to manually redraw parts of an image than to fix them in Photoshop.  
I mostly use Gemini for generating images (thanks Google for the free 20 images a day).

Has anyone found a good way around this?  
Any tools, workflows, or prompting tricks that help reduce the cleanup work?  
Or maybe there's a way to get cleaner generations from the start, with smoother linework and less color noise?

comments.author: SlightOfHand_
comments.body: Have you tried asking Gemini to clean up the image?

replies.author: RungerdH
replies.body:
Yes, but that doesn’t change a lot. Like here, there’s still no flat colors

https://preview.redd.it/bwn7bu320x4h1.jpeg?width=1024&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=664b11be9788a251a43cbe4c011d8003b1d79fef

replies.author: SlightOfHand_
replies.body: I’m not sure what you’re asking for, this looks like the colors are pretty flat to me. Do you mean you’re seeing a lot of like, pixel-level noise? Or is it a style thing like the output is too shiny/wrong colors/too many colors etc?

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: AI generated images only have the \*appearance\* of flat colors to the naked eye, but if you go and eyedrop them it's quite clear that they're not truly flat. So if you actually are looking for flat color aesthetic you have to manually paint or modify them (pixel art producers using AI use various processing methods to effectively compress colors into the allotted palette or tonemap it in processing. This is fairly mandatory if you actually want to  maintain consistency as a true pixel art project.

replies.author: SlightOfHand_
replies.body: Right, so my clarifying question was to determine whether the issue was at the design level or the pixel level. If its design level, it can be resolved by prompting, if its pixel level, it will be resolved by post-processing (and there’s various tools that can be used for this, or Claude etc can probably whip up a script that handles it fairly quickly)

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: I believe they were saying they liked the art style they were getting but the pixel colors were not coming out right ( hence their mention of "cleaning up color noise" rather than mentioning completely redoing the style.) But yes, if it was a style issue then most models respond very well to flat color prompts as long as they're not prompting conflicting lighting/shadows.

replies.author: EmotionalFan5429
replies.body: There are LoRAs for various Image Generation models (search here: https://civitai.com/search/models?sortBy=models\_v9&query=flat%20color). Maybe you can achieve the result with perfect prompt, but I wouldn't bet on that. ComfyUI, free models and LoRAs -- are the way!

comments.author: AggressiveHippo7296
comments.body:
https://3dtools.co.uk/imagecolorreduction/

Is pretty good for reducing the amount of colors down to whatever you want. :)

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: I found it took me just as long to clean up AI art to match my own aesthetic as it did to just draw from scratch since I use flat colors as well.  There are processing methods that can be automated by something like comfyui if your goal is to  refine the color noise and clamp down your pixel colors into a specific palette range. Or you can do it manually via Photoshop/Gimp using custom palettes and indexing the colors.  For actually taking advantage of this you do have to have a defined palette you're using repeatedly though... if it changes based on every image then  you're kind of just stuck with color ranging and replacing things anyway.
